mission_10: Congratulations on completing the causal inference chapter! You have implemented causal discovery algorithms that can learn causal structure from observational data. The PC algorithm uses conditional independence tests to build a DAG skeleton and orient edges via v-structures. LiNGAM exploits non-Gaussianity to identify causal direction, and ANM tests whether noise is independent of the cause. These methods complement the causal identification techniques you learned earlier — while do-calculus tells you whether an effect is identifiable given a DAG, causal discovery helps you learn the DAG itself. In practice, combine domain knowledge with data-driven discovery: use algorithms to suggest candidate structures, then validate them against known mechanisms. The complete causal inference toolkit — from DAGs to discovery — enables you to move from correlation to causation systematically.
